provenance.orgName: Mount Grace (in East Harsley), Yorkshire, Charterhouse of the Assumption of St Mary the Virgin
provenance.p: This attribution was rejected in both the first and second editions of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1941, 1964), which did not change in the Supplement (1987).

The corresponding Medieval Libraries of Great Britain index card is suggestive of Ker's evolving opinion over time, and he appears to have returned to this card at least twice to add further notes. The crux of the matter is the colophon: Scriptum finaliter in Monte gracie ultimo die mensis maii anno Domini Mᵒ CCCᵒ XIX. Deo gratias Eterna sapientia benedicat et custodiat corde et corpora vestra. When Ker originally wrote this index card, this colophon evidently seemed distinctive to him (and therefore suggestive of Mount Grace provenance). He wrote: 'For other manuscripts, none of which have this colophon, see J. E. Wells, Manual, p. 1353. Wells does not notice this copy.'

However, Ker's later additions to the index card suggest that he came to learn of other copies with the same colophon, implicitly weakening a potential Mount Grace attribution for MS 255. For example, he notes: 'The Brogyntyn MS (HMC ii 857) has the same colophon (letter from the librarian of the National Library of Wales, March 1948)'; 'but compare Ormsay Gore MS (HMC iv 379), no. 19, which has the same colophon.'

On this card, Ker also queries the date in the colophon: 'the date must be miswritten (? read M CCCC XIX)'. Compare his adjacent note on the card: 'Dom Justin McCann reports that this [i.e. M CCCC XIX] is the reading of the manuscript).
